recentItems.title: El Salvador Army Storms Haiti: Bukele's 'Gang War' Gets Port-au-Prince Cheer? Inside Americas Clash
recentItems.description:
This man called himself the 'World's coolest dictator'. The crime rate has reportedly fallen drastically during his tenure. We are talking about Nayib Bukele, President of El Salvador. Now, he has moved his fight to a country that doesn't even share a border with El Salvador. What made headlines in Central and South America recently was Bukele's move to send over 2,000 troops to Haiti—a country that has been struggling to overcome gang violence. Recently, Bukele shared a video of troops attacking a house where the leader of one of the most dreaded gangs in the country was reportedly hiding. It is interesting to note that Bukele was alerted about the gang leader hiding in the building through an X post. He asked, 'Where is the house?' He asked for the exact address and promised to destroy it. And within days, he did exactly that. Lanmo San Jou, or Wilson Joseph, the notorious gangster, was reportedly not present in that house. But 20 other alleged members of his gang reportedly lost their lives. This is not just a single instance of such an attack. A grand football stadium was reportedly captured by gang members. Bukele's men, along with Haitian authorities, reclaimed it. Guns were mounted on robodogs to counter the gangsters. Bukele even claimed that human skulls were found inside the stadium.
Now, the big question: Why is El Salvador's Bukele fighting a war in Haiti? What's really his agenda?
